references.geographic_scope: Cross-equatorial zonal-velocity section at35W. Mean observed EUC centered on the equator.
references.temporal_scope: Mean of16 ship sections across35W, with source sections spanning1990–2006; uneven cruise sampling, not a continuous or common-period annual climatology.

references.source_citation: Hormann and Brandt(2007), Atlantic Equatorial Undercurrent and associated cold tongue variability, J.Geophys.Res.112:C06026, doi:10.1029/2006JC003931.
references.source_locator: Section2.3.1.1 paragraph14/Figure1 for35W observed,FLAME,SPFLAME cores; Section3.1 paragraph22/Figure5 for10W FLAME core. Sections2.1 paragraphs7–8 and2.2 paragraph9 for experiment periods and observed section construction.
references.qualification: Observed,FLAME andSPFLAME means are separate evidence cases, not interchangeable or independent repeats of one observation. FLAME1990–2002 is an interannually forced output interval; SPFLAME last-two-spinup-year mean has no calendar-year assignment. The16-section observed mean is not the15-section transport subset or a hindcast-period mean. Above30m the observed mean is completed toward a surface-drifter climatology, not continuously sampled to0m.30–300m observed and31.5–310.6m model transport domains, isopycnals and10m near-surface model resolution do not define the EUC physical top/bottom, thickness or depth uncertainty. Only the two FLAME sections may support one common-model-period illustrative core trend; no observation/model blending, annual extrema, exact model core latitude, width join or volume.
